answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake: before an agent can trade, it must lock a deposit slashed for fraud, so spawning thousands of Sybils costs real money instead of being free. Trust then accumulates only from verified completed work, building slowly like layers of marble rather than from self-asserted claims. New identities earn small rewards, a drop of nectar at a time, only after independent peers confirm genuine delivery, and duplicate behavior is flagged like identical juniper cuttings planted in a row.
